18   parameter type                  req_t       = logic,                // AXI 4 request struct, with atop field

22   parameter logic [RespWidth-1:0] RespData    = 64'hCA11AB1EBADCAB1E, // Hexvalue for data return value
23   parameter bit                   ATOPs       = 1'b1,                 // Activate support for ATOPs.  Set to 1 if this slave could ever get an atomic AXI transaction.
24   parameter int unsigned          MaxTrans    = 1                     // Maximum # of accepted transactions before stalling
25 ) (

31   output resp_t slv_resp_o

15 //! AXI Package
16 /// Contains all necessary type definitions, constants, and generally useful functions.
17 package axi_pkg;
18   /// AXI Transaction Burst Type.
19   typedef logic [1:0] burst_t;
20   /// AXI Transaction Response Type.
21   typedef logic [1:0] resp_t;
22   /// AXI Transaction Cacheability Type.
23   typedef logic [3:0] cache_t;
24   /// AXI Transaction Protection Type.
25   typedef logic [2:0] prot_t;
26   /// AXI Transaction Quality of Service Type.
27   typedef logic [3:0] qos_t;
28   /// AXI Transaction Region Type.
29   typedef logic [3:0] region_t;
30   /// AXI Transaction Length Type.
31   typedef logic [7:0] len_t;
32   /// AXI Transaction Size Type.
33   typedef logic [2:0] size_t;
34   /// AXI5 Atomic Operation Type.
35   typedef logic [5:0] atop_t; // atomic operations
36   /// AXI5 Non-Secure Address Identifier.
37   typedef logic [3:0] nsaid_t;
38 
39   /// In a fixed burst:
40   /// - The address is the same for every transfer in the burst.
41   /// - The byte lanes that are valid are constant for all beats in the burst.  However, within
42   ///   those byte lanes, the actual bytes that have `wstrb` asserted can differ for each beat in
43   ///   the burst.
44   /// This burst type is used for repeated accesses to the same location such as when loading or
45   /// emptying a FIFO.
46   localparam BURST_FIXED = 2'b00;
47   /// In an incrementing burst, the address for each transfer in the burst is an increment of the
48   /// address for the previous transfer.  The increment value depends on the size of the transfer.
49   /// For example, the address for each transfer in a burst with a size of 4 bytes is the previous
50   /// address plus four.
51   /// This burst type is used for accesses to normal sequential memory.
52   localparam BURST_INCR  = 2'b01;
53   /// A wrapping burst is similar to an incrementing burst, except that the address wraps around to
54   /// a lower address if an upper address limit is reached.
55   /// The following restrictions apply to wrapping bursts:
56   /// - The start address must be aligned to the size of each transfer.
57   /// - The length of the burst must be 2, 4, 8, or 16 transfers.
58   localparam BURST_WRAP  = 2'b10;
59 
60   /// Normal access success.  Indicates that a normal access has been successful. Can also indicate
61   /// that an exclusive access has failed.
62   localparam RESP_OKAY   = 2'b00;
63   /// Exclusive access okay.  Indicates that either the read or write portion of an exclusive access
64   /// has been successful.
65   localparam RESP_EXOKAY = 2'b01;
66   /// Slave error.  Used when the access has reached the slave successfully, but the slave wishes to
67   /// return an error condition to the originating master.
68   localparam RESP_SLVERR = 2'b10;
69   /// Decode error.  Generated, typically by an interconnect component, to indicate that there is no
70   /// slave at the transaction address.
71   localparam RESP_DECERR = 2'b11;
72 
73   /// When this bit is asserted, the interconnect, or any component, can delay the transaction
74   /// reaching its final destination for any number of cycles.
75   localparam CACHE_BUFFERABLE = 4'b0001;
76   /// When HIGH, Modifiable indicates that the characteristics of the transaction can be modified.
77   /// When Modifiable is LOW, the transaction is Non-modifiable.
78   localparam CACHE_MODIFIABLE = 4'b0010;
79   /// When this bit is asserted, read allocation of the transaction is recommended but is not
80   /// mandatory.
81   localparam CACHE_RD_ALLOC   = 4'b0100;
82   /// When this bit is asserted, write allocation of the transaction is recommended but is not
83   /// mandatory.
84   localparam CACHE_WR_ALLOC   = 4'b1000;
85 
86   /// Maximum number of bytes per burst, as specified by `size` (see Table A3-2).
87   function automatic shortint unsigned num_bytes(size_t size);
88     return 1 << size;
89   endfunction
90 
91   /// An overly long address type.
92   /// It lets us define functions that work generically for shorter addresses.  We rely on the
93   /// synthesizer to optimize the unused bits away.
94   typedef logic [127:0] largest_addr_t;
95 
96   /// Aligned address of burst (see A3-51).
97   function automatic largest_addr_t aligned_addr(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size);
98     return (addr >> size) << size;
99   endfunction
100 
101   /// Warp boundary of a `BURST_WRAP` transfer (see A3-51).
102   /// This is the lowest address accessed within a wrapping burst.
103   /// This address is aligned to the size and length of the burst.
104   /// The length of a `BURST_WRAP` has to be 2, 4, 8, or 16 transfers.
105   function automatic largest_addr_t wrap_boundary (largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len);
106     largest_addr_t wrap_addr;
107 
108     // pragma translate_off
109     `ifndef VERILATOR
110       assume (len == len_t'(4'b1) || len == len_t'(4'b11) || len == len_t'(4'b111) ||
111           len == len_t'(4'b1111)) else
112         $error("AXI BURST_WRAP with not allowed len of: %0h", len);
113     `endif
114     // pragma translate_on
115 
116     // In A3-51 the wrap boundary is defined as:
117     // `Wrap_Boundary = (INT(Start_Address / (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length))) ×
118     //    (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length)`
119     // Whereas the aligned address is defined as:
120     // `Aligned_Address = (INT(Start_Address / Number_Bytes)) × Number_Bytes`
121     // This leads to the wrap boundary using the same calculation as the aligned address, difference
122     // being the additional dependency on the burst length. The addition in the case statement
123     // is equal to the multiplication with `Burst_Length` as a shift (used by `aligned_addr`) is
124     // equivalent with multiplication and division by a power of two, which conveniently are the
125     // only allowed values for `len` of a `BURST_WRAP`.
126     unique case (len)
127       4'b1    : wrap_addr = (addr >> (unsigned'(size) + 1)) << (unsigned'(size) + 1); // multiply `Number_Bytes` by `2`
128       4'b11   : wrap_addr = (addr >> (unsigned'(size) + 2)) << (unsigned'(size) + 2); // multiply `Number_Bytes` by `4`
129       4'b111  : wrap_addr = (addr >> (unsigned'(size) + 3)) << (unsigned'(size) + 3); // multiply `Number_Bytes` by `8`
130       4'b1111 : wrap_addr = (addr >> (unsigned'(size) + 4)) << (unsigned'(size) + 4); // multiply `Number_Bytes` by `16`
131       default : wrap_addr = '0;
132     endcase
133     return wrap_addr;
134   endfunction
135 
136   /// Address of beat (see A3-51).
137   function automatic largest_addr_t
138   beat_addr(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len, burst_t burst, shortint unsigned i_beat);
139     largest_addr_t ret_addr = addr;
140     largest_addr_t wrp_bond = '0;
141     if (burst == BURST_WRAP) begin
142       // do not trigger the function if there is no wrapping burst, to prevent assumptions firing
143       wrp_bond = wrap_boundary(addr, size, len);
144     end
145     if (i_beat != 0 && burst != BURST_FIXED) begin
146       // From A3-51:
147       // For an INCR burst, and for a WRAP burst for which the address has not wrapped, this
148       // equation determines the address of any transfer after the first transfer in a burst:
149       // `Address_N = Aligned_Address + (N – 1) × Number_Bytes` (N counts from 1 to len!)
150       ret_addr = aligned_addr(addr, size) + i_beat * num_bytes(size);
151       // From A3-51:
152       // For a WRAP burst, if Address_N = Wrap_Boundary + (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length), then:
153       // * Use this equation for the current transfer:
154       //     `Address_N = Wrap_Boundary`
155       // * Use this equation for any subsequent transfers:
156       //     `Address_N = Start_Address + ((N – 1) × Number_Bytes) – (Number_Bytes × Burst_Length)`
157       // This means that the address calculation of a `BURST_WRAP` fundamentally works the same
158       // as for a `BURST_INC`, the difference is when the calculated address increments
159       // over the wrap threshold, the address wraps around by subtracting the accessed address
160       // space from the normal `BURST_INCR` address. The lower wrap boundary is equivalent to
161       // The wrap trigger condition minus the container size (`num_bytes(size) * (len + 1)`).
162       if (burst == BURST_WRAP && ret_addr >= wrp_bond + (num_bytes(size) * (len + 1))) begin
163         ret_addr = ret_addr - (num_bytes(size) * (len + 1));
164       end
165     end
166     return ret_addr;
167   endfunction
168 
169   /// Index of lowest byte in beat (see A3-51).
170   function automatic shortint unsigned
171   beat_lower_byte(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len, burst_t burst,
172       shortint unsigned strobe_width, shortint unsigned i_beat);
173     largest_addr_t _addr = beat_addr(addr, size, len, burst, i_beat);
174     return _addr - (_addr / strobe_width) * strobe_width;
175   endfunction
176 
177   /// Index of highest byte in beat (see A3-51).
178   function automatic shortint unsigned
179   beat_upper_byte(largest_addr_t addr, size_t size, len_t len, burst_t burst,
180       shortint unsigned strobe_width, shortint unsigned i_beat);
181     if (i_beat == 0) begin
182       return aligned_addr(addr, size) + (num_bytes(size) - 1) - (addr / strobe_width) * strobe_width;
183     end else begin
184       return beat_lower_byte(addr, size, len, burst, strobe_width, i_beat) + num_bytes(size) - 1;
185     end
186   endfunction

188   /// Is the bufferable bit set?
189   function automatic logic bufferable(cache_t cache);
190     return |(cache & CACHE_BUFFERABLE);
191   endfunction
192 
193   /// Is the modifiable bit set?
194   function automatic logic modifiable(cache_t cache);
195     return |(cache & CACHE_MODIFIABLE);
196   endfunction

226       WBACK_RALLOCATE                   : return 4'b1111;
227       WBACK_WALLOCATE                   : return 4'b1011;
228       WBACK_RWALLOCATE                  : return 4'b1111;

250   /// RESP precedence: DECERR > SLVERR > OKAY > EXOKAY.  This is not defined in the AXI standard but
251   /// depends on the implementation.  We consistently use the precedence above.  Rationale:
252   /// - EXOKAY means an exclusive access was successful, whereas OKAY means it was not.  Thus, if
253   ///   OKAY and EXOKAY are to be merged, OKAY precedes because the exclusive access was not fully
254   ///   successful.
255   /// - Both DECERR and SLVERR mean (part of) a transaction were unsuccessful, whereas OKAY means an
256   ///   entire transaction was successful.  Thus both DECERR and SLVERR precede OKAY.
257   /// - DECERR means (part of) a transactions could not be routed to a slave component, whereas
258   ///   SLVERR means the transaction reached a slave component but lead to an error condition there.
259   ///   Thus DECERR precedes SLVERR because DECERR happens earlier in the handling of a transaction.
260   function automatic resp_t resp_precedence(resp_t resp_a, resp_t resp_b);
261     unique case (resp_a)
262       RESP_OKAY: begin
263         // Any response except EXOKAY precedes OKAY.
264         if (resp_b == RESP_EXOKAY) begin
265           return resp_a;
266         end else begin
267           return resp_b;
268         end
269       end
